provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Marks the far end of an approximate stretch of time or space, usually with から on the near end: 夕方から夜にかけて, 肩から背中にかけて. The sibling entries single out a field of ability (暗記にかけては) and stake something precious on a vow (名誉にかけて). The span is deliberately fuzzy and continuous, which suits weather, seasons, historical periods, and a spreading sensation; an exact cutoff or a deadline takes まで instead.

examples.ruby: 三月[さんがつ]から四月[しがつ]にかけて引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの依頼[いらい]が増[ふ]える。
examples.english: Moving requests pick up over the stretch from March into April.

examples.ruby: 肩[かた]から背中[せなか]にかけて鈍[にぶ]い痛[いた]みが続[つづ]いている。
examples.english: A dull ache runs from my shoulder on across my back and won't let up.

examples.ruby: 深夜[しんや]から明[あ]け方[がた]にかけて雨[あめ]が強[つよ]まる見込[みこ]みです。
examples.english: The rain is expected to intensify from late at night through toward dawn.

patterns.usage_note: Runs a range up to the point where an event occurs, taking a plain-form verb clause as well as a noun, and its までの form modifies a noun to name the whole stretch: 雨がやむまで待つ, 出発までの三日間. Sibling lanes cover the rest: how far an action itself extends over a noun (駅まで歩く), the cap on an allowance (一人二枚まで), and 〜までだ for a fallback plan (やり直すまでだ). The far end here is a definite boundary, where にかけて leaves it vague.

examples.ruby: 日[ひ]が暮[く]れるまで子[こ]どもたちは川辺[かわべ]で遊[あそ]んでいた。
examples.english: The children played by the river right up until the sun went down.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]がやむまで軒下[のきした]で少[すこ]し待[ま]つことにした。
examples.english: I decided to wait a little under the eaves until the rain let up.

examples.ruby: 出発[しゅっぱつ]までの三日間[みっかかん]は毎日[まいにち]買[か]い物[もの]に出[で]かけた。
examples.english: For the three days leading up to departure I went out shopping every day.

patterns.usage_note: Holds the end point up as a striking or exhaustive extreme: everything from A right down to B (衣装から小道具に至るまで), or a state that has persisted all the way to now (現在に至るまで). The register is formal and written; plain まで keeps the same boundary but loses the sense of how far the range extends. Like まで it takes a noun or a plain-form verb (話すに至るまで).

examples.ruby: あの事件[じけん]は現在[げんざい]に至[いた]るまで解決[かいけつ]していない。
examples.english: That case remains unsolved right up to the present day.

examples.ruby: 衣装[いしょう]から小道具[こどうぐ]に至[いた]るまで全[すべ]て手作[てづく]りだ。
examples.english: Everything is handmade, from the costumes down to the smallest prop.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]が事故[じこ]のことを話[はな]すに至[いた]るまで何年[なんねん]もかかった。
examples.english: It was years before my grandmother came to speak about the accident.

patterns.usage_note: A directional variant of にかけて: the へ keeps a sense of motion toward the far end, so it suits spans that trace a path or spread in one direction (中腹から頂上へかけて, 幕末から明治へかけて). にかけて is much more frequent and is the unmarked choice for most spans. The same string also occurs literally as へ plus 掛ける or 駆ける, which is unrelated to this pattern.

examples.ruby: 山[やま]の中腹[ちゅうふく]から頂上[ちょうじょう]へかけて紅葉[こうよう]が進[すす]む。
examples.english: The autumn colors creep up from the mountainside toward the summit.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]の東側[ひがしがわ]から川[かわ]へかけて古[ふる]い商店街[しょうてんがい]が続[つづ]く。
examples.english: An old shopping street runs from the east side of the station over toward the river.

examples.ruby: 幕末[ばくまつ]から明治[めいじ]へかけて西洋[せいよう]の技術[ぎじゅつ]が流入[りゅうにゅう]した。
examples.english: Western technology poured in across the years from the late Edo period into Meiji.
